unitKey: 2Solid, liquid, gas states and changes of stateChemistry

questions.question: At what temperature does water boil and also condense under standard conditions?
What is steam?
options: Water in the solid state
Water in the liquid state
Water in the gas state
A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen gas

questions.question: What happens to the volume of a substance when it changes from a liquid to a gas by boiling?
options: Its volume increases
Its volume decreases
Its volume stays exactly the same
Its volume becomes zero

questions.question: How do particles behave when a substance condenses?
options: They move further apart
They move closer together
They stop moving completely
They increase in size

questions.question: What change occurs to a Bunsen burner flame when you open the air hole?
options: It changes from a hot blue flame to an orange sooty flame
It changes from an orange sooty flame to a hotter, cleaner blue flame
It changes from a green flame to a yellow safety flame
The flame goes out immediately

questions.question: If you need to light a Bunsen burner in a science laboratory, where should you light your splint from?
options: The nearest Bunsen burner that is already lit
A match at the teacher's desk only
The gas tap directly
A Bunsen burner on the far side of the room

questions.question: How should a lit splint be carried safely across a laboratory?
options: Pointing directly upwards with both hands
Angled slightly downwards and shielded by the other hand
Waving it gently from side to side to keep it lit
Angled upwards and held as high as possible

questions.question: Which statement correctly compares the energy of different states of matter for a substance?
options: Gas states have the least energy, solids have the most
Liquids have the most energy, gases have the least
Solids have the least energy, gas states have the most
Solids, liquids, and gases all have the same amount of energy

questions.question: Which of the following is true about evaporation?
options: It can only happen at a substance's boiling point
It can happen at temperatures below a substance's boiling point
It only happens when a substance is freezing
It requires the liquid to reach 100°C to start

questions.question: How does temperature affect the rate at which water evaporates?
options: The hotter the water, the more slowly it evaporates
Temperature has no effect on the speed of evaporation
The hotter the water, the more quickly it evaporates
Water only evaporates when it is cooled down

questions.question: What state change occurs when a substance melts?
options: It changes from liquid to gas
It changes from gas to solid
It changes from solid to liquid
It changes from liquid to solid

questions.question: What state change occurs when a substance freezes?
options: It changes from liquid to solid
It changes from solid to liquid
It changes from gas to liquid
It changes from liquid to gas

questions.question: For a pure substance, how do its melting point and freezing point compare?
options: The melting point is always higher than the freezing point
The melting point is always lower than the freezing point
They are the same temperature
They have no relationship to each other

questions.question: What holds the particles in fixed positions when a substance is in its solid state?
options: Gravitational forces between the particles
Forces of attraction between the particles
The high energy of the particles
Air pressure pushing them together

questions.question: Describe the particles in a liquid state.
options: They are held in rigid, fixed positions and cannot move
They are held together but have enough energy to break free to move around
They have no forces holding them together and are very far apart
They move in straight lines without ever touching each other

questions.question: How does the strength of the force of attraction between particles affect a substance's melting point?
options: The stronger the force of attraction, the higher the melting point
The stronger the force of attraction, the lower the melting point
The strength of the force of attraction does not affect the melting point
Stronger attractions prevent substances from ever melting

questions.question: Which set of temperatures correctly identifies the freezing point of water, typical room temperature, and normal human body temperature?
options: Water freezes at 100ºC, room temp is 37ºC, body temp is 20ºC
Water freezes at 0ºC, room temp is 20ºC, body temp is 37ºC
Water freezes at 0ºC, room temp is 37ºC, body temp is 100ºC
Water freezes at -10ºC, room temp is 20ºC, body temp is 37ºC

questions.question: Which of these is a property of a substance in its gas state?
options: It has a fixed shape and cannot flow
It cannot be compressed and has a fixed volume
It can flow, fills the whole of a container, and can be compressed
It can flow but cannot be compressed

questions.question: What is present in the space between the particles in a gas?
options: Air
Water vapour
Nothing at all
Tiny dust particles

questions.question: Which statement describes the properties of a substance in the liquid state?
options: It has a fixed shape, does not flow, and cannot be compressed
It can flow, fills the shape of its container, and cannot be compressed
It can flow, fills the whole container, and can be compressed
It has a fixed shape, can flow, and can be compressed
